# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 13 (Bu-Vb Np13)
**ID:** Bu-Vb Np13
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 13

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
*Dvebhāga* constitutes the thirteenth training rule of the *Nissaggiya Pācittiya* (relinquishment with confession) class in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* of the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule regulates the composition of wool blankets, establishing that a Buddhist monk who makes a blanket containing more than fifty percent black wool incurs an offense requiring both the forfeiture of the blanket and formal confession [SuttaCentral]. Modern translations cataloged on SuttaCentral include an English rendering by Bhikkhu Brahmali among versions in four other languages [SuttaCentral].
This training rule is attested across all surviving early Buddhist monastic lineages. Curated parallels exist in the Theravāda *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* and *Parivāra*, as well as the Prātimokṣa sūtras and Vinayavibhaṅgas of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Lokottaravāda, and Dharmaguptaka traditions preserved in Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus registers substantial formulaic Pali-internal text reuse (505 matches across 94 texts), displaying the highest concentrations of shared phrasing with adjacent rug- and robe-making rules, notably *Nissaggiya Pācittiya* 12, 11, 15, 7, and 14, along with the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language automated alignments, DharmaNexus reports correspondences with Tibetan Vinaya texts—chiefly the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-2) and the *Pratimokṣasūtravṛtti* (D4107)—agreeing with the Mūlasarvāstivāda parallels recorded by SuttaCentral [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
